claim: A* with a consistent heuristic never reopens nodes, and Theorems 2-3 of Hart, Nilsson and Raphael (1968, read from the original) show it expands no more nodes than any admissible algorithm no more informed than it (up to tie-breaking). The theorems assume consistency and positive arc costs. LLM scores have no lower-bound guarantee.
agent_test: Design limit: LLM scoring has no admissibility guarantee; measure overestimation rate of scores.
audit_note: Wikipedia is a derivative source (the Dechter-Pearl point lives there); the primary check is Hart et al. 1968 pp.104-105 viewed as page images: Lemma 2 and Theorem 2 assume consistency and delta graphs, Theorem 3 handles ties. 'LLM scores have no lower-bound guarantee' is the researcher's inference.

claim: LLM-scored ranking of children (breadth-limited search over thoughts) beats sampled chain of thought at similar token cost on short puzzles: Game of 24 GPT-4 CoT 4.0%, CoT best-of-100 49%, ToT b=5 74%. Caveat from gap search: the cost row for CoT best-of-100 is $0.47 (49%) and ToT $0.74 (74%) (re-read on the PDF image); with GPT-3.5 ToT lags self-consistency at equal budget (Wang 2024), and AB-MCTS shows plain repeated sampling matching or beating standard MCTS on ARC-AGI at equal calls.
agent_test: Ranked children vs best-of-k at equal total tokens on our tasks.

claim: Code-based search with LLM-written successor and goal test solves all 1362 Game of 24 instances, so the ToT gain shows search helps, not that LLM scoring is required.
agent_test: Compare LLM-scored ranking vs code-checked successor and goal test at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: In LLM tree search the bottleneck is generation, not evaluation: GPT-4 generator with GPT-3.5 evaluator 64%, GPT-3.5 generator with GPT-4 evaluator 31%, GPT-3.5 both 19%, GPT-4 both 74%.
agent_test: Vary generator and ranker strength separately at equal tokens.

claim: Search over a model-scored tree helps agents on long tasks and gains grow with budget: VisualWebArena 18.9 to 26.4% (+39.7% relative), WebArena 15.0 to 19.2% (+28.0%); 200-task subset 24.5% to 37.0% at c=20.
agent_test: Expansion budget vs success on our agentic tasks.

claim: Pruning and backtracking both matter: 5x5 crosswords ToT 60% word level; no backtrack 20%; no prune 41.5%. The model evaluator prunes real solutions at times.
agent_test: Ablate prune and backtrack in our scaffold.

claim: A learned scorer beats prompting the model to score itself (TS-LLM; Q* real table cells: GSM8K best-of-N(QVM) 74.5 vs Q* 78.8 and 80.8, MATH 46.8 vs 49.1 and 54.3 vs 55.4, MBPP 75.0 vs 77.0). Small models' self-reward is near random (RAP with random reward on LLaMA2-7B GSM8K: 24.34 vs 22.67 to 22.90). Q* gains over best-of-N are about 1 to 6 points.
agent_test: Self-prompted scoring vs a small trained scorer; training is outside the schema, note only. Independence weak.
audit_note: Table cells match (GSM8K 74.5 vs 78.8/80.8, MATH 46.8 vs 49.1 and 54.3 vs 55.4, MBPP 75.0 vs 77.0; RAP random-reward 24.34 vs 22.90/22.67), but those numbers give Q* gains of 1.1 to 6.3 points (GSM8K PRM+QVM +6.3), not 'only 1 to 4'.
claim_before_audit: A learned scorer beats prompting the model to score itself (TS-LLM; Q* real table cells: GSM8K best-of-N(QVM) 74.5 vs Q* 78.8 and 80.8, MATH 46.8 vs 49.1 and 54.3 vs 55.4, MBPP 75.0 vs 77.0). Small models' self-reward is near random (RAP with random reward: GSM8K 24.34 vs 22.67 to 22.90). Q* gains over best-of-N are only 1 to 4 points.

claim: Model value plus search helps: RAP lifts LLaMA-33B on 6-step Blocksworld from 0.00 (CoT) to 0.42, matching GPT-4 CoT at 0.40; removing the LM heuristic from LATS drops HotPotQA EM from 0.63 to 0.37. Whether the gain shrinks for stronger base models was not tested in these papers.
agent_test: Check whether gains vanish with our strongest base model.
audit_note: Numbers match (RAP LLaMA-33B 6-step CoT 0.00 vs RAP(20) 0.42, GPT-4 CoT 0.40; LATS no-LM-heuristic 0.37 vs 0.63), but neither paper compares search gains across base-model strength, so 'gain shrinks for strong base models' is an inference from comparing RAP on a 33B model with GPT-4 CoT.
claim_before_audit: Model value plus search helps, but the gain shrinks for strong base models: RAP Blocksworld LLaMA-33B 6-step 0.00 (CoT) to 0.42, GPT-4 CoT already 0.40; LATS removing the LM heuristic drops HotPotQA EM 0.63 to 0.37.

claim: LLMs alone plan poorly: GPT-4 about 34% valid on 600 Blocksworld; o1-preview 97.8% on plain, 52.8% obfuscated, 37.3% randomised, 23.63% on 110 plans of 20+ steps; Fast Downward 100% at 0.12 s.
agent_test: Plain vs obfuscated planning items at equal tokens. o1 lines share one paper family.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: External verifier loops raise planning success: VAL back-prompting reaches 82% Blocksworld in 15 rounds and 70% Logistics, but only about 10% on Mystery Blocksworld. Same authors as the main planning critiques.
agent_test: Add or remove a checker at equal tokens.

claim: Chain-of-thought hints help planning only when tailored to the problem class and collapse as size grows (Blocksworld stacking GPT-4 3.8% zero-shot vs 59.3% specific CoT).
agent_test: Test the scaffold on sizes beyond the prompt examples.

claim: Asking the LLM once per domain for heuristic code and running sound greedy best-first search beats end-to-end LLM planning and hFF: 720 tasks, R1 373, V3 343, Gemini 305, hFF 234, best LLM planning 174; generation cost $0.25 to $6.12.
agent_test: Agent writes a scoring function for children, then uses it without more LLM calls.
audit_note: Minor: heuristic selection samples several heuristics per domain and picks the best on training tasks; Tuisov et al. (400 tasks, 20 domains) is a separate smaller replication in the same direction.

claim: Per-node LLM calls are costly: calling GPT-4 on all 50,143 expanded Blocksworld states would take about 14 days and over $1000; ToT used up to about 100 calls per Game of 24.
agent_test: Count scoring calls per ranked child.

claim: Heuristic errors hurt most near the goal; an LLM heuristic trained on middle nodes is often inadmissible and gives shorter search with worse solutions (Middle: ILR 9.74, 56.69% optimal).
agent_test: Always report answer quality with cost when comparing rankers.

claim: A learned LLM heuristic only pays for its inference cost on hard problems: inverse time ratio Sokoban OOD 2.4 to 2.7, Sokoban IID about 0.26, maze about 0.002.
agent_test: Rank only above a difficulty threshold; test it.

claim: Training on search traces with mistakes beats solution-only training: Searchformer Sokoban 93.7% optimal with up to 26.8% fewer steps than its A* teacher; Stream of Search Countdown 51.27% vs 25.73%.
agent_test: Not for a scaffold; at most show traces in context.
audit_note: Minor: 93.7% is the optimal-solution rate (solved 95.5-96.0); the 26.8% is average shorter search dynamics of the final model.

claim: LLM waypoints can cut A* work: LLM-A* 50x30 grids GPT-3.5 operations 57.39% and storage 74.96% of A*, +2.44% path length; the other LLM A* paper expands 352 vs 372 nodes but paths are longer (34 vs 27).
agent_test: Small effect; do not rely on it.
audit_note: Minor: the 352 vs 372 nodes and 34 vs 27 path length are the Aisle map only; the other maps show 133 vs 145 and 197.67 vs 210 nodes.

claim: An LLM as commonsense prior inside MCTS beats the LLM policy alone on household tasks (unseen scenes 82.9 vs 74.3 on simple tasks); plain UCT gets 0%.
agent_test: Low priority.

claim: Diversity of candidate plans predicts search gains: PlanSearch pass@200 77.0% vs repeated sampling 60.6% (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, LiveCodeBench).
agent_test: Measure diversity vs gain in our candidate generator.

claim: Heuristic-quality theory, now opened: Helmert and Roger 2008 (error 1 still forces exponential A* work on GRIPPER, MICONIC) and Wilt and Ruml 2012 (greedy ranking is fast only when h correlates strongly with true distance-to-go; percent error and h-h* rank correlation do not predict failure). Korf 1997 and Dechter-Pearl 1985 not opened.
agent_test: Read the sources before use.
audit_note: Minor: Wilt and Ruml's tested explanations (percent error, h-h* correlation) are rejected on the paper's domain set, and 'Hanoi 29.47 vs inverse tiles 29.49' in the notes is a mix-up of unit tiles; the claim's wording is unaffected.

claim: Environment feedback (ReAct) beats plain CoT on grid path planning (GPT-4 96.1% success; CoT loses 7% with 4+ obstacles).
agent_test: Environment feedback vs none.

claim: Under equal budget, simple self-consistency matches or beats many multi-sample strategies; ToT only wins with a strong base model (GPT-4 on Game of 24) and loses to SC with GPT-3.5. At equal calls with test feedback, plain repeated sampling matches or beats standard MCTS (ARC-AGI 15.0/18.6 vs 9.0/14.0; LiveCodeBench 37.8 vs 36.7 for GPT-4o). No test of ToT-style search with 2025-26 reasoning models was found.
agent_test: Always run a best-of-N or SC arm at equal tokens against ranked-children search.

claim: Process-reward-ranked beam search beats best-of-N only at small budgets and on harder questions; at large budgets it can fall below best-of-N and it hurts on easy questions (PaLM 2 on MATH). A width-allocating PRM tree search (REBASE) beats sampling and MCTS at equal FLOPs.
agent_test: Use search only on hard items; cap breadth and depth; stop early when top branches agree.
audit_note: Minor: Snell says beam search over-optimizes on easy bins 1-2 at higher budgets (not strictly 'hurts' at all budgets).

claim: Step-level (process) scorers beat outcome scorers and majority voting: MATH best-of-1860 PRM 78.2, ORM 72.4, majority 69.6; at 256 outputs (Mistral-7B MetaMATH) the ReST-MCTS value model beats self-consistency by 3.6 (GSM8K) and 3.9 (MATH500) points and Math-Shepherd by 3.2 and 2.2. Gaps among step scorers are small (0.4 to 1.7).
agent_test: Score steps, not only final answers; a cheap scorer may be enough.
audit_note: Lightman (78.2/72.4/69.6) and the 0.4-1.7 step-scorer gap match, but in ReST-MCTS Table 3 Math-Shepherd beats SC by only 3.2 (GSM8K) and 2.2 (MATH500); the ReST-MCTS value model beats SC by 3.6 and 3.9.
claim_before_audit: Step-level (process) scorers beat outcome scorers and majority voting: MATH best-of-1860 PRM 78.2, ORM 72.4, majority 69.6; Math-Shepherd and ReST-MCTS value beat SC by about 4 points at 256 outputs. Gaps among step scorers are small (0.4 to 1.7).

claim: Self-rating by LLMs is a weak ranker: GPT-3.5 direct evaluation on balanced right/wrong answers is at chance (50.6%), GPT-4 78.75%; GPT-4 is near random on TheoremQA; as a binary verifier GPT-4 throws away right answers (false negative 95.8% graph coloring, 97.1% Mystery Blocksworld, 20.7% Game of 24) while accepting few wrong ones (false positive 0.5% to 18.55%). Small models rank near random (rStar).
agent_test: False accept (overestimate) is rarer than false reject; do not let a self-critique prune solutions without a sound check.
audit_note: Minor: 'GPT-4 near random on TheoremQA' is shown only graphically; the 18.55% false positive belongs to Blocksworld and 0.5% to Mystery Blocksworld, consistent with the stated range.

claim: Greedy or heavily weighted ranking fails when the score orders nodes by the wrong thing: greedy works when h-to-distance Spearman is 0.52 to 0.997 and fails at 0.39, 0.34, -0.03, 0.16 (Wilt and Ruml 2012); percent error and h-h* rank correlation do not separate working from failing domains.
agent_test: Measure rank correlation of child scores with true steps-to-solve on dev items before using greedy selection; keep width above 1.

claim: Even a nearly perfect heuristic (error 1) leaves A* with exponential work on GRIPPER and MICONIC; better scoring does not remove the blowup on tasks with many interleavable independent subproblems.
agent_test: Add decomposition or symmetry pruning rather than expecting better scoring to fix combinatorial tasks.

claim: A small cheap evaluator keeps most of the gain: ToT b=5 with GPT-4 proposer and GPT-3.5 evaluator 72% for $33.53 vs GPT-4 evaluator 76% for $159.87 (Game of 24); small 7B PRMs in MCTS match o1-level math (rStar-Math) but they are trained, not prompted.
agent_test: Use a weaker model or a yes/no prompt to rank children; check on our tasks.

claim: Stopping rules on voting save most samples with little loss: ESC cuts samples 33.8% (MATH) to 84.2% (Coin Flip); Adaptive-Consistency up to 7.9x with under 0.1% average accuracy drop. Search gains saturate near 64 trajectories on MATH (rStar-Math).
agent_test: Stop expansion when the top candidates agree; spend more on items where they do not.
audit_note: Minor: the Adaptive-Consistency 7.9x / under 0.1% figure is from Aggarwal et al. (arXiv 2305.11860, abstract), not from the ESC paper listed as its source; rStar-Math shows saturation or slow gain at 64 trajectories on MATH, AIME, Olympiad Bench but not College Math.

claim: Where exact checks exist (tests, proofs), repeated sampling turns coverage into accuracy (SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% with 250 samples); without a verifier, voting and reward-model selection plateau after about 100 to several hundred samples. The ranker is the bottleneck.
agent_test: Prefer a sound check over an LLM score wherever one exists.

claim: Q* table cells re-read from the PDF image: the earlier doubt is resolved (74.5 is best-of-N(QVM) and 65.2 is the base on GSM8K). Q* beats best-of-N by +4.3 GSM8K, +2.3 and +1.1 MATH, +2.0 MBPP; one run, no variance.
agent_test: Treat Q* as a small, unreplicated edge.

claim: Humans plan with heuristic best-first search and plan deeper with expertise (four-in-a-row; abstract only read). No measured human heuristic error rates or admissibility data found; Newell and Simon 1972 not opened.
agent_test: Gap 10 remains open.
